title: Can Climate Change Affect Our Mental Health?

blanks.sentence: Disasters such as floods and wildfires can destroy _____.
People in affected areas may experience _____.
Trauma involves very bad and _____ emotional effects.
The expert describes climate trauma as _____ rather than merely private.
Individuals with stronger _____ from family are generally more resilient.
Resilience is also linked to _____ with the community.
One positive result was work on a _____.

multipleChoice.question: What is the main point made about climate trauma?
options: It is mostly a medical condition treated by individuals alone.
It happens only when people directly lose their homes.
It is less serious than other effects of climate change.
It affects communities and therefore needs collective recovery.

multipleChoice.question: Which factor is linked with greater resilience after climate-related disasters?
options: Avoiding discussion of the disaster within the family.
Feeling supported by family and connected to the community.
Moving away from the affected area as quickly as possible.
Depending mainly on expert treatment rather than neighbours.

multipleChoice.question: How does the interviewer respond to the expert’s community-based explanation?
options: She finds the idea especially noteworthy and interesting.
She doubts whether community healing can happen after disasters.
She treats the explanation as obvious and unimportant.
She shifts the focus away from mental health entirely.

multipleChoice.question: Why can strong community ties help people after disasters?
options: They prevent natural disasters from damaging homes.
They remove the need for families to offer support.
They make people more able to recover from difficulty.
They guarantee that trauma will disappear immediately.

multipleChoice.question: What contrast is drawn between climate trauma and individual trauma?
options: Climate trauma is short-term, while individual trauma lasts longer.
Climate trauma affects whole communities, not only separate people.
Climate trauma is caused by emotions, while individual trauma is physical.
Climate trauma is solved by experts, while individual trauma is solved locally.

multipleChoice.question: What view of rebuilding is suggested in the discussion?
options: Repairing social connections is part of the healing process.
Rebuilding should focus on buildings rather than relationships.
Communities recover best when people work separately.
Emotional recovery is unrelated to community structure.

multipleChoice.question: In the phrase about how “it rebuilds and reknits together”, what does “it” refer to?
options: A psychiatric condition.
A single survivor’s home.
A support organisation.
The affected community.

multipleChoice.question: What can be inferred from the wildfire survivor’s volunteer work?
options: He wanted to leave the damaged town permanently.
He thought the fire had made community work unnecessary.
He turned personal loss into efforts to strengthen the area.
He believed only children needed support after the fire.

multipleChoice.question: Why are the children mentioned in the survivor’s description?
options: To show that children were unaffected by the wildfire.
To illustrate that resilience spread across the community.
To explain why the community plaza was built for schools.
To compare young people’s trauma with adults’ trauma.

multipleChoice.question: What overall implication does the discussion leave?
options: Climate change affects property more than mental wellbeing.
Community recovery is useful only after the physical rebuilding ends.
Collective support can help people cope with climate-related trauma.
Natural disasters create stronger communities without extra effort.
